title: Unions: Memory Overlaps
goal: Learn how Rust unions store fields at the same memory location.

sections.text: You know unions from C or C++, where multiple fields share the exact same memory address. Rust supports unions using the `union` keyword.

sections.caption: All fields in a union start at memory offset zero.

sections.text: Unlike enums, unions do not store a discriminant tag to track which field is active. Constructing a union and writing to its fields are safe operations.
Reading a field from a union requires an `unsafe` block. The compiler cannot check if the memory contains valid data for the requested field type.

sections.code:
let d = Data { integer: 42 };
let val = unsafe { d.integer };
sections.caption: Reading a field requires unsafe because Rust cannot verify the tag.

sections.text: Reading a union field outside an `unsafe` block produces compiler error `E0133`.

explanation: Learn how Rust unions store fields at the same memory location.
